questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid staring at one spot for too long.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to keep to the right to avoid a hazard ahead. Drivers must follow the rules on regulation signs like this one.

questions.question: Where can drivers not park?
questions.explanation: You cannot park on bridges, overpasses, underpasses, or in tunnels.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You can pass if you know the road ahead.
You can pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. Drivers must obey it. When you see this sign, you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or taking other drugs. It is dangerous to yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:

options.text: All occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Make sure everyone in your vehicle wears a seat belt. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object that can hurt everyone in the car.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather, as they may be going too fast.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be traveling too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: What happens to drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They lose control of their body, mind, and vehicle.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They lose control of their body, mind, and vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and body. It hurts your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with drugs?

options.text: The effects of both become weaker.
The effects of both become stronger.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both effects stronger. It is dangerous to drive after drinking alcohol or taking drugs, and even more dangerous when you mix them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Drive slowly into a roundabout and let traffic already in it go first.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: You are at a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, or a person signals you to stop. Only cross if you are sure no train is coming. Never race a train.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop or back up on the highway. Do not cross lanes suddenly or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: North Dakota law requires headlights to be on:

options.text: When the temperature drops below freezing.
During the day in good weather.

questions.explanation: North Dakota law requires headlights to be on between sunset and sunrise. Use low beams instead of high beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle within 300 feet.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching for items, reading, or daydreaming while driving. If a driver near you seems distracted, stay away from them because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Do what other drivers are doing, even if the crossing guard says something different.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the rules you would use if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always follow instructions from crossing guards, signs, and police in school zones. Slow down and drive carefully when directed to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Look carefully for traffic crossing in front of you.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check both your mirrors and your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Slow down, move to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down and move your car to give the emergency vehicle a clear path. Then stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.
